events.title: Howard Carter Opens Tutankhamun's Burial Chamber
events.description: British archaeologist Howard Carter officially unsealed the burial chamber of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings, revealing the sarcophagus within its nested golden shrines.
events.significance: The discovery of the nearly intact royal tomb became one of the most celebrated archaeological finds in history and sparked worldwide fascination with ancient Egypt.

events.title: Lithuania Declares Independence
events.description: The Council of Lithuania signed the Act of Independence in Vilnius, proclaiming the restoration of an independent Lithuanian state based on democratic principles after years of Russian imperial and German wartime control.
events.significance: The date is celebrated as Lithuania's Restoration of the State Day and marks the foundation of the modern Lithuanian state, which was later re-established in 1990 after Soviet occupation.

events.title: Fidel Castro Sworn In as Prime Minister of Cuba
events.description: Following the overthrow of Fulgencio Batista in the Cuban Revolution, Fidel Castro took office as Prime Minister of Cuba, beginning his long period of rule over the island nation.
events.significance: Castro's leadership transformed Cuba into a socialist state aligned with the Soviet Union, shaping Cold War geopolitics, including the Cuban Missile Crisis and decades of strained US relations.

events.title: Kyoto Protocol Enters into Force
events.description: The Kyoto Protocol, an international treaty committing industrialized nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, became legally binding after Russia's ratification brought it past the required threshold.
events.significance: It was the first major international agreement setting binding emission reduction targets and laid the groundwork for later climate accords such as the Paris Agreement.

events.title: Birth of Philipp Melanchthon
events.description: German theologian and scholar Philipp Melanchthon was born in Bretten. He became a close collaborator of Martin Luther and the principal author of the Augsburg Confession.
events.significance: Melanchthon was a key intellectual architect of the Protestant Reformation and reformed German education, earning the title 'Teacher of Germany'.
